subject: Post-call recap: Redwood integration & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Lee <sam.lee@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-18T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: Redwood integration & next steps

Hi Sam —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so the team is aligned and we have clear next steps. If I missed anything please flag it.

Pain points you highlighted:
- Inference latency spikes on peak queries (goal: p95 < 200ms for core user flows)
- Unpredictable per-token cost across different model variants and cloud regions
- Need for private data handling: on-prem/VPC option for sensitive content and strict audit logs

Goals we agreed on:
1) Reduce latencies for search & chat flows to meet p95 < 200ms in prod
2) Pilot an embeddings + reranking flow to improve relevance and reduce calls to expensive large models
3) Short PoC (4 weeks) using Redwood Private or Dedicated depending on network/procurement constraints

Integration areas we discussed (initial scope):
- SDK changes: lightweight client stub to support streaming responses and function/tool-calling patterns. We'll provide TypeScript and Python examples.
- Function calling: structured tool invocation for your downstream actions (ticket creation, enrichment) — we discussed a JSON schema-first approach.
- Streaming & structured outputs: stream tokens for UI responsiveness and include structured JSON outputs for deterministic parsing.
- Embeddings + reranking: batch embedding generation (GPU-accelerated) and a reranking step using FAISS/Annoy; scope to test recall/latency tradeoffs.
- Quantization & perf: recommend int8 quantization profile for the pilot model to balance latency/cost.

Attachments: I attached the integration spec and a draft mutual action plan (MAP) that outlines milestones, owners, and success criteria.

Immediate next steps / owners:
- [Marissa] Send SOC2 and compliance artifacts + HubSpot deal link (today) — ACTION: marissa_cole
- [Dev] Share a short SDK demo video and sample repo with function-calling examples (by 2027-04-22) — ACTION: dev_patel
- [Acme] Confirm procurement timeline and whether Private (VPC/on-prem) is required for the PoC (by 2027-04-21) — ACTION: Sam / Jenna
- [All] Align on success metrics for the 4-week PoC (latency SLA, throughput targets, and qualitative relevance improvements) — ACTION: all

Proposed PoC timeline: Week of 2027-05-03 start, 4 weeks, with a mid-point demo after 2 weeks.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick sync if you want to run through the MAP live.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: redwood_integration_spec.pdf, mutual_action_plan.xlsx
From: Sam Lee <sam.lee@acmecorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-18T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Redwood integration & next steps

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. That matches our notes. A few quick clarifications/questions:

- Procurement: I've looped in Jenna Ortiz (cc'd) who owns vendor onboarding and procurement. Targeting an internal review by 2027-04-28 but that depends on the level of documentation we get (SOC2, architecture, and DPAs).
- PoC env: We prefer to start on Dedicated if Private onboarding will push past our timeline; can you outline the differences in setup effort between Dedicated and Private for a 4-week pilot?
- Embeddings: We like the idea of reranking but want to understand token count and expected per-query cost with a 2k query corpus.

Also, procurement will want an estimate of committed spend vs burst capacity pricing. Can you include both in the MAP?

Happy to move forward — we tentatively hold the week of 2027-05-03 for the kick-off pending procurement.

Best,
Sam
Head of Search & Relevance, Acme Corp
sam.lee@acmecorp.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Lee <sam.lee@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Jenna Ortiz <jenna.ortiz@acmecorp.com>
Date: 2027-04-19T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Redwood integration & next steps

Sam / Jenna —

Great, thanks for the fast reply. Quick answers and links below:

- Documentation: attaching SOC2 and a compliance pack; also linking to our SOC2 report (internal link in MAP).
- Dedicated vs Private:
  * Dedicated: fastest to stand up (1–3 days), reserved GPU pool, data isolated at tenant level but still in our managed control plane — good for speed.
  * Private (VPC/on-prem): longer set-up (2–4 weeks typically), customer-managed network, full audit logs and KMS control — recommended if you have strict regulatory requirements.

I updated the MAP to include both pricing scenarios (committed vs burst). See the attached MAP and the HubSpot deal for line item estimates.

For embeddings: initial estimate for a 2k query corpus using mid-size models (embedding-512) — embedding generation one-time cost and reranking per-query cost: we put ballpark numbers in the MAP; Dev will follow up with more precise token estimates and batching recommendations.

Next steps I will take now:
- Upload SOC2 & compliance bundle to the HubSpot deal and the shared MAP link.
- Dev will publish a sample repo with a streaming SDK example + function-calling JSON schema tomorrow.

Can we confirm a 30-min technical kickoff with Dev and Dylan on 2027-05-03 or 2027-05-04? I can send a calendar invite once you confirm.

Thanks,
Marissa

Attachments: redwood_integration_spec.pdf (updated), mutual_action_plan.xlsx

- A README with recommended quantization profiles (int8) and notes on Dedicated vs Private runtime differences

I'll ping Sam & Jenna once it's up so they can validate assumptions before the kickoff.
